# laravelcloud_background_processes (Resource)

Manages a background process on a Laravel Cloud instance.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "laravelcloud_background_processes" "example" {
  processes = 1
  type      = "worker"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance` (String) The instance this resource belongs to.
- `processes` (Number)
- `type` (String)

### Optional

- `background_process` (String) The background process identifier
- `command` (String) Custom command to run. Required when type is 'custom'. Not applicable for 'worker' type.
- `config` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config))

<a id="nestedatt--config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config`

Optional:

- `backoff` (Number) Number of seconds to wait before retrying a failed job. Only applicable for 'worker' type background processes.
- `connection` (String) The queue connection name. Only applicable for 'worker' type background processes.
- `force` (Boolean) Force the worker to run even in maintenance mode. Only applicable for 'worker' type background processes.
- `queue` (String) The queue name(s) to process. Can be comma-separated for multiple queues. Only applicable for 'worker' type background processes.
- `rest` (Number) Number of seconds to rest between jobs. Only applicable for 'worker' type background processes.
- `sleep` (Number) Number of seconds to sleep when no jobs are available. Only applicable for 'worker' type background processes.
- `timeout` (Number) Number of seconds a job can run before timing out. Only applicable for 'worker' type background processes.
- `tries` (Number) Number of times a job should be attempted. Only applicable for 'worker' type background processes.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import laravelcloud_background_processes.example instance-id/the-id
```
